title: English Football League (EFL)
summary: Designed a comprehensive match centre and CMS solution to elevate the fan experience and improve the content authoring workflow for club staff.
indexTeaser: Delivering a full-cycle fan experience—from pre-match previews to live reporting—while providing club authors with a powerful, streamlined content management system.

oversight.blurb: EFL sought a long-term digital partner to ensure the fan experience was second to none. The project focused heavily on the 'match centre' and required integrating various third-party services to provide timely, detailed, and consistent content for all clubs.

problem.heading: The Problem Statement
problem.body:
The project faced two major pain points.

The Fan Experience — the old legacy club websites lacked modern appeal. Fans needed real-time updates and consistent information during live events.

The Authoring Experience — club staff had to use too many different, disparate software applications to cover a single matchday, leading to process fragmentation, duplication of effort, and slow reporting turnarounds.

images.caption: The fan experience and the authoring exprience had to align.
The authoring experience HAD to work in realtime, during a live match.

decision.heading: The Strategy
decision.body: The strategy was to build a unified digital experience around the 'pulse of the match'—making sure that content was available, structured, and optimised for the three key stages: pre-match, during the match, and post-match. This required integrating the fan experience directly into the content creation workflow.

images.caption: The pulse of the match meant rendering realtime updates before, during and after the match.

methods.heading: Approach
methods.body: The approach combined observation, data mapping, and usability testing to create a cohesive solution that served both fans and content authors.

steps.title: User Interviews & Observational Research
steps.description: Speaking with users and observing multiple matches to understand the required content at different phases of the match—before, during, and after.

steps.title: Information Architecture Mapping
steps.description: Structuring the content flow for the match centre, ensuring consistent visibility of statistics and news across all 58 clubs.

solution.heading: The Solution Delivered
solution.body:
A robust, integrated platform with two complementary halves.

The Fan Experience — a seamless, multi-stage journey providing all necessary pre-game guides, real-time match statistics, and post-match reports.

The Authoring Solution — a redesigned CMS allowing authors to write notes, schedule content, and publish real-time updates directly in a single, mobile-friendly environment.

images.caption: The final comprehensive match centre experience starting from the home page and leading the user through club form, match previews, live match updates and post-match reports.

outcomes.heading: Impact & Outputs
outcomes.body: The result was a scalable framework for 58 clubs, demonstrating a fluid and continuous user experience. The outcome included a fully functional design system and a comprehensive technical specification for the CMS. The impact continues to drive revenue and fan engagement across the league.

reflection.heading: Reflection
reflection.body: The main takeaway was the importance of editorial decision-making. While the technical design was successful, greater involvement in the editorial components would have allowed for a more holistic and positive impact on the overall digital story.
